title: kbext.py rehearse takes a planted fork and a group overlay from one upstream ext tag to the next and reports no conflict, no shipped file edited and every extender verified
goal: kbext.py rehearse --upstream URL --from TAG --to TAG --team DIR [--fork] runs in temporary directories it removes: a clone at TAG (with --fork, a planted fork commit adding a group root by kbroot.py add) with DIR's group settings, then kbgit.py upstream to TAG; it prints the conflicting paths, the shipped files the group's setup changed and kbext.py verify's lines, exit 0 only when all three are empty or ok, 1 otherwise. --plant builds the upstream itself from the running checkout's tracked tools as two commits tagged ext-v<API_VERSION> and a next minor, and --plant --break makes the second a planted removal of the lane point without a major version, which rehearse reports by name. This is the epic's proof.

run:
import subprocess,sys,tempfile,pathlib
t=pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/"grp-kb"
r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbext.py","init-team",str(t),"--group","grp","--upstream","git@corp.example.com:kb/it-ops-kb.git"],capture_output=True,text=True); assert r.returncode==0, r.stderr
k=lambda *a: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbext.py","rehearse","--plant","--fork","--team",str(t),*a],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=900)
r=k(); assert r.returncode==0, (r.stdout[-2000:],r.stderr[-2000:])
r=k("--break"); assert r.returncode==1 and "lane" in r.stdout+r.stderr, (r.returncode,r.stdout[-2000:])
